title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（鎌田洋研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Kamada Hiroshi)
keywords: Problem discovery and problem solving, CDIO
educationalGoal: Students are giving the opportunity to summarize all of their university studies based on what students have learned to date by identifying a unique theme, thinking about problems related to it, and then developing a process for proposing solutions. Students are expected to integrate the knowledge, technology, sensibility, and logical thinking skills of the media technology and media design fields that have been acquired thus far to become creative engineers who contribute to the AI information society.
advice:
Project Design III is based on the contents of classes from the first to third years of the Department of Media Informatics Studies. This is a culmination of four years of university life, in which students practice problem finding and problem solving techniques and build deliverables based on the advice of their faculty adviser.
Learning advice: Project Design III is an eight-credit, full-year course. Students will work on their chosen themes over the course of an entire year to achieve deliverable results. To that end, proper self-management greatly affects the results. Knowing about yourself, developing your strengths and finding ways to overcome your shortcomings are very important. These techniques will surely be useful when going out into society.
requiredKnowledge: All prerequisite courses of this department must already be completed. Be able to summarize what you have learned from the first to third years. Students are expected to have mastered problem finding and solving methods through experience in project design subjects and specialized seminars up to the third year.

Be able to apply specialized expertise to the set project theme.
Be able to perform CDIO-based research and development on the set project theme.

lessons.content:
Each week, students will report to each other
on the progress of their individual research
themes and the results of the study of given
issues. Students are expected to help each
other improve their respective research contents
 through discussions. Students will make
presentations on- and off-campus, as
appropriate, in terms of results. An
intermediate review is conducted during the 7th
or 8th week of the first semester. An
intermediate presentation will be made at the
end of the first semester.
(200 min x 15 weeks）

lessons.content:
Each week, students will report to each other
about the progress of each research theme and
the results of the study of given issues.
Students are expected to help each other
improve their respective research contents
through discussions. Students will make
presentations on- and off-campus, as
appropriate, in terms of results. An
intermediate review is conducted during the 7th
or 8th week of the second semester. Finally,
two general exercises will be introduced. The
research results will be summarized by
December, all documents will be completed by
January, and they will be presented at the
public presentation review meeting.
(200 min x 15 weeks)
